$readme: THE CLAIM LEDGER — every obligation the shipped guidance owes the agent.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The skill, the five protocol references, the four
dispatch briefs and the worker code standards are PROSE: an obligation
lives in a sentence, and a sentence can be reworded, merged, or deleted
without anything failing. A compression pass that drops one prohibition
looks exactly like a compression pass that dropped a filler word.
So the obligations are extracted ONCE, as ATOMIC claims with a stable id,
and every one of them is checked by
packages/mcp/test/skill/skill-claim-ledger.test.mjs. A claim may be
REWORDED — the matcher is written against the obligation, not the wording
— but it may not DISAPPEAR, and it may not WEAKEN.
HOW TO USE IT:
- compression: reword freely, then run the ledger; if a matcher stops
matching, either the obligation was lost (fix the text) or the
obligation MOVED to another file (move the claim too, and say so in
the same commit).
- a NEW obligation: add a claim with the next free id. The ledger
grows when the system grows, and never shrinks silently.
- a DELETED obligation: delete the claim in the same commit. The diff
is the record. CI shows it; a reviewer sees it.
MATCHER: a regular expression, tested against the file's text. It is
written to match the obligation's LOAD-BEARING WORDS, not a whole
sentence, so a reword that preserves the rule still passes.
